Epoch 0: pretrained CordsNet-R8 vs monkey N¶

Frozen pretrained model, val split (1,854 images, batches of 64 from one day). CKA per model layer, brain area and 10 ms bin.

  • CKA_0: usual linear CKA (training-loss form of rounds 3/4)
  • CKA_S: Song et al. 2012 (corrects for the finite number of images); main metric
  • CKA_C: Chun et al. 2025 (also corrects for the finite number of electrodes)
  • All three are pooled over batches: H values (numerator, two denominators) averaged over batches first, then one ratio
  • Error bars: SE from resampling batches (bootstrap)
  • NaN = undefined (deep layers in the first bins: all images still give the same spontaneous activity)

Inputs: Round1/outputs/epoch0_pretrained/results.npz (copied from Torch), raw monkey N npz files in ~/Desktop/neural_data (Figure 3 only).

In [1]:
import warnings
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from pathlib import Path

warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", category=RuntimeWarning)   # nanmean over all-NaN bins, 0/0 in undefined bins

ROUND1 = Path("~/Desktop/DynVision/CordsNet/Round1").expanduser()
RESULTS = ROUND1 / "outputs" / "epoch0_pretrained" / "results.npz"
NEURAL = Path("~/Desktop/neural_data").expanduser()

r = np.load(RESULTS)
layers, areas, ests = [[str(x) for x in r[k]] for k in ("layers", "areas", "estimators")]
t_ms = r["bin_start_ms"] + 5                    # bin centers
days = r["batch_day"]
h_num, h_dm, h_dn = r["h_num"], r["h_den_model"], r["h_den_neural"]
# h_num (batch, layer, area, bin, [naive, Song]); h_dm (batch, layer, bin, [naive, Song, Chun]); h_dn (batch, area, bin, 3)

# pooled CKA (layer, area, bin, estimator): CKA_0 = naive / naive, CKA_S = Song / Song, CKA_C = Song / Chun
cka = r["cka_pooled"]
S = ests.index("CKA_S")

# response windows: from response onset to 200 ms (monkey N time courses)
window = {"V1": np.arange(3, 20), "V4": np.arange(3, 20), "IT": np.arange(7, 20)}

# best layer per area: highest CKA_S in the response window
best = {area: int(np.nanargmax(np.nanmean(cka[:, j, window[area], S], axis=1))) for j, area in enumerate(areas)}

est_color = {"CKA_0": "#2a78d6", "CKA_S": "#eb6834", "CKA_C": "#1baf7a"}
area_color = {"V1": "#2a78d6", "V4": "#eb6834", "IT": "#1baf7a"}
day_color = ["#2a78d6", "#eb6834", "#1baf7a", "#eda100"]
layer_color = ["#86b6ef", "#6da7ec", "#5598e7", "#3987e5", "#2a78d6", "#256abf", "#184f95", "#0d366b"]

print(f"{h_num.shape[0]} batches, days {sorted(set(days.tolist()))}")
print("best layer by CKA_S (response window):", {a: layers[i] for a, i in best.items()})

27 batches, days [1, 2, 3, 4]
best layer by CKA_S (response window): {'V1': 'layer2', 'V4': 'layer2', 'IT': 'layer8'}

1. Which layer matches each area?¶

CKA averaged over bins, for every layer. Top: all 20 bins. Bottom: response window only (V1, V4 30-200 ms; IT 70-200 ms). Error bars: SE from 1,000 bootstrap resamples of the batches.

In [2]:
# bootstrap over batches: resample batches, pool H values, recompute CKA and its mean over bins
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
nb, n_boot = h_num.shape[0], 1000
boot = np.zeros((n_boot, 2, len(layers), len(areas), 3))           # (resample, [all bins, window], layer, area, estimator)
for k in range(n_boot):
    idx = rng.integers(0, nb, nb)
    num, dm, dn = h_num[idx].mean(0), h_dm[idx].mean(0), h_dn[idx].mean(0)
    c = np.stack([num[..., 0] / np.sqrt(dm[:, None, :, 0] * dn[None, :, :, 0]),
                  num[..., 1] / np.sqrt(dm[:, None, :, 1] * dn[None, :, :, 1]),
                  num[..., 1] / np.sqrt(dm[:, None, :, 2] * dn[None, :, :, 2])], axis=-1)
    for j, area in enumerate(areas):
        boot[k, 0, :, j] = np.nanmean(c[:, j], axis=1)
        boot[k, 1, :, j] = np.nanmean(c[:, j, window[area]], axis=1)
se = np.nanstd(boot, axis=0)

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(13, 7), sharex=True)
for row, label in enumerate(["all 20 bins", "response window"]):
    for j, area in enumerate(areas):
        ax = axes[row, j]
        b = np.arange(20) if row == 0 else window[area]
        for e, est in enumerate(ests):
            ax.errorbar(range(1, 9), np.nanmean(cka[:, j, b, e], axis=1), yerr=se[row, :, j, e], fmt="o-",
                        color=est_color[est], lw=2, ms=6, capsize=3, label=est)
        ax.set_title(f"{area}, {label}")
        ax.set_xticks(range(1, 9))
        ax.grid(alpha=0.3)
    axes[row, 0].set_ylabel("CKA")
for ax in axes[1]:
    ax.set_xlabel("model layer")
axes[0, 0].legend()
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

print("Response window, mean CKA per layer (layer1 ... layer8), +- bootstrap SE for the best layer:")
for j, area in enumerate(areas):
    for e, est in enumerate(ests):
        y = np.nanmean(cka[:, j, window[area], e], axis=1)
        i = int(np.nanargmax(y))
        print(f"  {area} {est}: best {layers[i]} ({y[i]:.3f} +- {se[1, i, j, e]:.3f})   " + "  ".join(f"{v:.3f}" for v in y))

The bottom 3 graphs: V1/v4 time window from 30ms to 200ms, chosen based on MonkeyN neural activations (neural activities begins only after 30ms for V1 and V4). and for IT it is from 70-200ms.

Each point answers: across the entire 200ms time window, on average how similar each CordsNet layer is to monkey's V1, V4, IT layer. This tells us we should try align: V1 with Layer 2, V4 with Layer 7, and IT ith Layer 8.

2. CKA over time¶

CKA_S per bin, one line per layer (light = layer1, dark = layer8). Gray: response window.

In [3]:
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(15, 4.2), sharey=True)
for j, area in enumerate(areas):
    ax = axes[j]
    ax.axvspan(window[area][0] * 10, 200, color="0.92", zorder=0)
    ax.axhline(0, color="0.5", lw=1)
    for i, layer in enumerate(layers):
        ax.plot(t_ms, cka[i, j, :, S], "-", color=layer_color[i], lw=2, label=layer)
    ax.set(title=f"{area}: CKA_S", xlabel="time after image onset (ms)", xlim=(0, 200))
    ax.grid(alpha=0.3)
axes[0].set_ylabel("CKA_S")
axes[-1].legend(fontsize=8, ncol=2)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

x-axis: time after image onset. y-axis: per bin CKA_S.
Grey area: chosen reaction time window.
CKA averaged across all batches.

For all three brain regions, CKA_S are all 0 before brain starts to react to the images. For V1, in the beginning all layers are equally similar, but as time went on only shallow layers align better. For V4, there is relatively small differences across all 8 layers. For IT, at later time steps deeper layers have higer CKA, but not as high as V1.

Interestingly for all 3 layers, we see a bump at 45ms.

3. Response timing: model layers vs brain areas¶

Mean activity over time, scaled so that the first bin = 0 and the peak = 1. Model: mean recorded activity of each layer (val images). Brain: mean MUA over all trials and electrodes of all 4 days (V1 without channels 320-383).

In [4]:
neural_tc = {}
for area in areas:
    total, n = np.zeros(20), 0
    for f in sorted(NEURAL.rglob(f"monkeyN_day*_{area}_binned.npz")):
        mua = np.load(f)["binned_mua"]
        if area == "V1":
            mua = np.delete(mua, np.arange(320, 384), axis=2)
        total += mua.sum(axis=(1, 2))
        n += mua.shape[1] * mua.shape[2]
    neural_tc[area] = total / n

model_tc = r["model_timecourse"]                                           # (layer, bin)
model_n = (model_tc - model_tc[:, :1]) / (model_tc.max(axis=1, keepdims=True) - model_tc[:, :1])

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 4.2), sharey=True)
for i, layer in enumerate(layers):
    axes[0].plot(t_ms, model_n[i], "o-", color=layer_color[i], lw=2, ms=4, label=layer)
for area in areas:
    c = neural_tc[area]
    axes[1].plot(t_ms, (c - c[0]) / (c.max() - c[0]), "o-", color=area_color[area], lw=2, ms=4, label=area)
axes[0].set(title="Model layers", xlabel="time after image onset (ms)", ylabel="normalized activity")
axes[1].set(title="Monkey N", xlabel="time after image onset (ms)")
for ax in axes:
    ax.grid(alpha=0.3)
    ax.legend(fontsize=8)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

print("Time to half of the peak (bin center, ms):")
for i, layer in enumerate(layers):
    print(f"  {layer}: {t_ms[np.argmax(model_n[i] >= 0.5)]}")
for area in areas:
    c = neural_tc[area]
    print(f"  {area}: {t_ms[np.argmax((c - c[0]) / (c.max() - c[0]) >= 0.5)]}")

Time to half of the peak (bin center, ms):

V1 removed the problematic channels.
Normalized per layer/ brain region activities over time.
For the model layers activities are normalized so that at 0ms activity is 0, and at the activation peak activity is 1.
For the model layers, we take the average activity across each bin (10ms, 5 time steps), and plot average activity per bin.

We see progressively delayed response as we go deeper into CordsNet layers, which aligns with CordsNet delays t_feedforward = 2ms between layers.

4. Three CKA estimators¶

Best layer per area (highest CKA_S in the response window), CKA over time with each estimator (all pooled over batches).

In [5]:
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(15, 4.2), sharey=True)
for j, area in enumerate(areas):
    i = best[area]
    axes[j].axhline(0, color="0.5", lw=1)
    for e, est in enumerate(ests):
        axes[j].plot(t_ms, cka[i, j, :, e], "o-", color=est_color[est], lw=2, ms=4, label=est)
    axes[j].set(title=f"{area} vs {layers[i]}", xlabel="time after image onset (ms)", xlim=(0, 200))
    axes[j].grid(alpha=0.3)
axes[0].set_ylabel("CKA")
axes[0].legend()
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Per bin CKA after image onset:

  • CordsNet model image onset begins the 200ms (0 to 100ms idle steps, 100 time steps)

  • CKA computed using validation set (1854 images, 64 images per batch, on the same day)

  • 0-25ms, CKA_S and CKA_C = 0, which is what we want to see

    • Because from figure 3, right, neural activity begins after 25ms, so before 25ms it's just random noise. On the model side however there is already systematic processing of image contents; random vs. systematic, CKA near 0 is expected.

  • See how CKA_0, from 0-25ms has high CKA: due to the diagonal impact!

  • CKA_0 is also misleading, if we look at the left most figure, at around 45ms where CKA_S and CKA_C are the highest, CKA_0 is the lowest.

  • We should go with CKA_S

5. Check: consistency across recording days¶

Best layer per area, CKA_S over time, pooled over the batches of each day separately.

In [7]:
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(15, 4.2), sharey=True)
for j, area in enumerate(areas):
    i = best[area]
    axes[j].axhline(0, color="0.5", lw=1)
    for k, d in enumerate(sorted(set(days.tolist()))):
        sel = days == d
        y = h_num[sel, i, j, :, 1].mean(0) / np.sqrt(h_dm[sel, i, :, 1].mean(0) * h_dn[sel, j, :, 1].mean(0))
        axes[j].plot(t_ms, y, "-", color=day_color[k], lw=2, label=f"day {d} ({sel.sum()} batches)")
    axes[j].set(title=f"{area} vs {layers[i]}: CKA_S by day", xlabel="time after image onset (ms)", xlim=(0, 200))
    axes[j].grid(alpha=0.3)
axes[0].set_ylabel("CKA_S")
axes[0].legend(fontsize=8)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

For day 4 there is only 3 batches of images, so we expect larger fluctuations of yellow curve.
